items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: The first funeral I played with Eddie Jackson was on this side of the river.

ctx.x: Well, people engaged here more than us. People saw... stuff

I don't know anybody who would be the best friend, but you didn't get the opportunity to get off. That's when you were. Did you hear Johnny Dawes when you were married? I was Johnny Dawes. I was Johnny, I was Jimmy Newman, Charlie McQuirties, and he was one of the best. I was the man George Backing, he was one of the best. I was his brother. He was a kid, he was a kid. The first funeral I played with Eddie Jackson was on this side of the river. I was working with Eddie Jackson at what they call a music hall. I…

But he couldn't play no more. He was way up, way up by the protection of the levy. And he'd see you sick. He'd have that coat on, that cap, as I must care for you. He loved his music. He was a bass player. John Smith was a pimp. He had a lot of women dressed very good. He was in Ace Blossom, one of the Zulus Club. He was a band-girl. Wood-Jill Trump, sometimes called him. Sometimes he was a friend I named Homer. He lived on the main. Jetson was called the same block as the high court. He was in Jetson. He signed…

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: I even played it with, uh, Eddie Jackson's tuxedo.

ctx.x: You don't remember how old it was, huh?
No. I knew I played it with a lot of brass bands. I played it with the Eureka. I even played it with, uh, Eddie Jackson's tuxedo.
